summary: # Marvelous Designer 2024.0: Dragón Parte 2 ## Introduction Let's continue with the development of the dragon's appearance. After modeling the hair cards, it's time to apply some textures. ## Texture Application I have created part of the fur in mesh using Xgen. I'm going to render using an orthographic view from above, in 4K resolution using Arnold. Returning to Marvelous Designer, for the workflow with the hair cards, we must first design the UVs. It is better to design the UVs in Marvelous Designer, since all 2D patterns can also be treated as UVs. ### UV Design For the face, I would like to keep the design, so I'm manually organizing the UVs in a square. Select the UV pieces, right-click, and adjust from 0 to 1. Select the remaining UV pieces and use the automatic UV packing function to adjust them to the V10 coordinates. ### Hair Card Grouping For the hair card, since I have created five types of fur, I am going to group strips of similar length in the same group, thus creating five groups. We assign the texture maps to the corresponding channels. We change the rotation of the texture map to zero. The texture mapping method should also be changed from repeated to unified. We stretch the UVs to adjust to the fur. ## Mustache Modeling For the dragon's mustache, it is also modeled in mesh and exported to OVJ files. Import the OVJ file to the scene as trim for the type of object. Use the glue function located in the upper right corner of the gizmo to limit it to the fabric. We adjust the rotation. We do the same with the right mustache. Select them and change the color to red and the material color to velvet. ### Simulation Check Let's see if the restrictions work. We start the simulation and drag the pattern of the nose. The trim or accessory moves with the fabric. This can create a natural movement animation during the recording of the animation cache. ## Working on Hairpins Next, we work on the hairpins. We open the hairpin window where we have all the tools. Use the free hairpin tool. Double-click on a point to add hairpins to the entire line. By default, in Marvelous Designer, there are six different hairpins. I'm going to use the Overlock hairpin and increase the width, length, and thickness. We will also change the color. ### Downloading Hairpin Styles You can download more styles of hairpins from the Connect store or register your own OVJ file to use it as a hairpin. For the eyelid, I'm going to apply the satin hairpin Demon downloaded from the Connect store. Change the color to gold and the type of material to silk. ### Applying Hairpins to Facial Features Apply the same hairpin used for the eyebrow to the part of the nose. Use the Rise hairpin downloaded from the Connect store for the lip, under eye, and upper eye. We will correct the edges of the side pattern and the inner lines of the hairpin. Use the Alexander Macbook Pencil to cover or to survive the parts of the hairpin. ### Edge Correction Remember to use the Extend option in the emergency window. Apply an Overlock hairpin on all the inner lines and contours of the hairpin. Change the color to make it more distinguishable. ## Skin Material For the skin of the head, I'm going to use the Artan Moteado fabric material. You can find it in the Substance folder in the library. In personalized properties, increase the size of the pattern and change the colors. ## Modeling the Body Bones Model the body bones in mesh, paired and animated to pose the dragon. The reason why I use disks like bones is based on the references of real life. In the Dragon Dance, the body also has disks as support structures. A poster is added to the bottom of each disk, and a person controls the poster to perform the movements. ### Exporting Animation The animation is exported as an Alembic cache when importing to Marvelous Designer. In Marvelous Designer, we import the Alembic file with the animation cache. We can preview the animation in the animation editor. ## Circular Pattern Creation We create a circular pattern with the same disk. After all the circular patterns are in position in the 3D window, use the pin tool to fix all the points on the edge of each circle. Once all the circle patterns are in position, use incentives. Do not force the wheel by the toolbar. ### Positioning Points To this end, unique Remote Set the point of the button which will optimize the extension of the real disk. After that, try to locate play on the exported dimensions inside the line that you created in one of the pins and choose to fix all the pins to the avatar to limit it to the animated mesh. ## Rectangular Piece Modeling Model a rectangular piece with the circumference of the circle for the width. The height will be the same as I used in mesh, which would be 1000 millimeters. A simple way to rely on the design in the 3D window is to create your own positioning point. ### Creating Positioning Points Let's go to the main menu, avatar editor. In the positioning, we add a new position. Place it between the two disks and turn it. Increase the length x and y. Also, add a point and assign it to the position we just made. We activate the positioning points. ### Sewing and Simulating We select the rectangular piece and click on the positioning point that we have just created. We sew this embossed pattern to the circle. I switch the pre-established settings of the fabric to the nylon bias and simulate. Copy and paste this pattern several times to fill the entire body of the dragon. ## Finalizing Animation Once the modeling is finished, use the animation editor to simulate the transition and be able to pose the dragon. Make sure that all the pins are connected to the avatar. Change the simulation quality to stable animation. We deactivate the collision with the ground and gravity. We also increase the air amortization to 3 and the time distortion in the scene to 2. ### Recording Animation Cache After that, we simply click on the record button and let Marvelous Designer do the entire animation cache for you. This would be the complete animation cache. And here would be the dragon posed and ready to export.
